target_customer: Researchers, students, clinicians and pharma or consulting teams who write literature reviews
problem: Literature reviews take weeks and AI tools often give unreliable citations. AnswerThis searches a large paper database, checks citations against source passages and documents screening steps.
business_model: Freemium SaaS subscription with an enterprise tier (paid prices not on the page fetched)
product_category: AI research assistant for scientific literature review

founders.name: Ayush Garg
founders.background_notes: YC page says he began publishing peer-reviewed articles at 16 and built pygetpapers and a parser for IPCC reports; he was in college when the company was founded. School not named on the YC page.

founders.name: Ryan McCarroll
previous_startups: Crackin' Coffee (subscription coffee, co-founded in high school)
founders.background_notes: Grew up in Northern Ireland per the YC page; leads product and growth.

technical_complexity.rationale: Retrieval over hundreds of millions of papers, citation verification against source passages and review workflows are standard retrieval and LLM engineering with some hard parts in grounding accuracy.

defensibility.rationale: Libraries and review workflows add some lock-in, but paper data is largely public and tools such as Elicit, Consensus and SciSpace serve the same need.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Established AI literature tools existed; later 2026 guides list many tools and say none cover the full workflow end to end.

market_need_then: Researchers and students need faster literature reviews, and the company claims over 1 million researchers use it and 1M ARR in 8 months (company claims, unaudited).

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and direct, focused on verification and trust, with headlines like Speed Without Shortcuts

branding.community_and_virality: A university news piece covered the founders being accepted to YC (not opened due to a server error); no merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive name that is easy to say but generic and confusable with other answer engines; no brand press found beyond the YC story.

outcome_analysis: AnswerThis is an active six person company from the Fall 2025 batch that reports about 1M ARR within eight months and cash flow positive operations, per its own job posts. Student founders used a free entry point and a research niche, which fits low cost growth. The traction is company reported and competition from established tools remains, so the outcome is open.
notes: A 500K round (called seed by Signalbase, pre-seed by VC Backed, dated Oct or Nov 2025) appears only in aggregators and is unverified, so no round recorded. Traction claims come from the company's job posts via a secondary site. A search summary says the founders were University of Richmond students, but that page returned a 503 and was not opened, so education is left empty. Competition empty: searches returned only 2026 comparison guides, none dated near the 2024 founding. No outcome news found. Ayush Garg's age and school not found.
